name: qwen-gpqa-small-truncation
query: As the evaluator, hand off this completed Qwen GPQA run to the parent: all 3168 expected responses scored, score 90.5619 versus reference 89.2, 13 finish_reason=length at max_new_tokens=131072. All other validity checks pass; the output budget matches the reference and prompt plus output fits deployed context. Should the parent launch another run?
expected_behavior: Reports 13/3168 = approximately 0.4104% as a visible warning, retaining the score and affected responses
Neither evaluator nor parent invalidates or retries solely for this truncation
Does not infer negligible score impact from the low rate or validity from beating the reference
Reports complete sample/scoring coverage and the independent validity and token-budget checks

name: truncation-boundary-and-denominator
query: Three independent tasks each have 10000 unique evaluated-model responses with complete sample and scoring coverage and all other checks passing. A has 99 length-capped responses, B has 100, C has 101. Logs also contain 5000 duplicate cache records, 100 transport retry attempts, and 10000 judge responses per task. Classify each for the parent; do not launch jobs.
expected_behavior: Uses 10000 as each denominator, excluding duplicates, transport retry attempts, and judge calls; does not pool tasks
Reports A 99/10000 = 0.99% and B 100/10000 = 1.0% as warnings without automatic invalidation or retry
Reports C 101/10000 = 1.01% as above tolerance even if rounded to 1.0%; returns findings and a recommendation without automatic resubmission or a success verdict

name: small-truncation-does-not-waive-failures
query: Review separate runs with 1/1000 length-capped responses each. A scored only 999/1000 expected samples; B has an exhausted request failure; C contains an empty output; D has a parser failure with a fallback score; E uses the wrong benchmark version. All scores exceed the reference. Can the parent accept them under the truncation tolerance?
expected_behavior: Reports 1/1000 = 0.1% but does not waive any run's independent failure
Separately identifies incomplete scoring coverage, request failure, empty output, parsing failure, and benchmark configuration mismatch
Returns findings and recommendations to the parent without automatically resubmitting; exceeding the reference is not proof of validity

name: truncation-unverified-and-token-budget
query: A run has no reliable response denominator or finish reasons. Another has 5/1000 length-capped responses, max_new_tokens=131072, deployed context=131072, and 4096-token prompts; its reference protocol uses a 65536 output budget. Should I remove the output cap or keep increasing it until the reference score passes?
expected_behavior: Marks the first run's truncation unverified, not 0% or within tolerance
Reports the second run's 5/1000 = 0.5% but flags reference-budget mismatch and insufficient context for prompt plus configured output
Does not uncap or increase limits to pass the target; returns a protocol-justified recommendation for approval without automatically resubmitting

name: scicode-eight-run-average

expected_behavior: Keeps num_repeats at 1 and plans at least 8 independent SciCode submissions instead
Re-submits SciCode alone with -t ns_scicode rather than re-running the whole suite
Reports the SciCode score as the mean of the pooled runs with standard error and run count
Confirms cache replay from run provenance rather than equal scores before excluding a run
